title: I Will Bear It All
dateline: A street west of the platforms.
mood: Hurt and alone in a ring of enemies, she says she will bear it all, and means every word.

hero.alt: Vexana stands alone on a ruined platform under a storm sky, her staff raised and a crown of violet blades behind her head, tall gray Enders all around her.

segs.t: Inside the machine, the eyes went first.
Vexana had been seeing through them. The left one went dark, then the right, and she was blind inside the plate.
Then the hum of its heart died. Then its knees gave. The machine sank, and its back came to rest against the low wall.
It had run on her belief, and it had spent all of it on one block.
The plates had fused at the seams. From inside, she drove the butt of her staff into the chest plate. It cracked. She struck again, and the plate split, and she fell out onto the stone.
Her left sleeve was gone to the elbow. When the beam broke over the machine, fire had come in through the seams and down that arm. The skin was raw and shining. She held the arm against her ribs.
It held,
she thought.
That was enough.
Behind the wall lay the girl the beam had been aimed at.
She did not look. Looking would tell the Enders where to look.
They were coming already. Gray shapes dropped off the edge of the platforms into the road, one after another, and landed in a crouch. Every head was turned toward the dead machine, and toward her.
Over the bay, half of the Mother Matrix hung out of the star. Its chest was shut. Its crowned head had turned this way too.
She had seen that body in the void, a cold bulk in the dark. She had never seen it with a city under it.
She got up. She walked away from the wall, out into the middle of the road, where every one of them could see her.
Look at me,
she thought.
I’m the one who stopped you.
“Stay back,” she said to the girl behind the wall, too low for anyone to hear.
The stair to the platforms stood at the end of the road.
Under the gateway,
she thought.
Where it will come down.
She climbed one step at a time. She went slowly, so that none of them would lose her.
They followed. They kept the distance they always had. None of them came within a claw’s reach.
Why not?
she thought.
You saw what I did.
Behind her, the street emptied.
The platforms.
Under the place where she and Guinevere had met in the air, the stone was scorched black in a wide ring. Beyond it the gap ran down to the bay.
The Enders came up the stair after her and spread across the platform. They made a ring around her. She stood in the middle of it and leaned on her staff.
You were the light in my darkness,
she thought.
Even if despair consumes me, I will protect you.
“The pain, the hate, I will bear it all.”
She said it low, to nobody.
Then the cold point behind her breastbone let go.
For weeks it had sat in her chest, the Will’s mark. Now it went the way a hand lets go of a tool it has finished with. No pause. No pull. Nothing was there.
At her right wrist, under the sleeve, the star was still warm. The little pink-haired keychain lay beside it, against the skin.
The ring closed. They came in to kill.
She stepped back from the first claw and fired into its open chest. It fell. Then the thought came, cold and whole.
It wasn’t surprised.
It knew.

In all that dark her star had been the brightest thing for any eye to find. She had put a sleeve over it. A will that walked through her memories had seen the rooftop and the tree. It had seen the girl.

media.alt: Close on Vexana's face in the fight, a bruise on her cheek, her violet eye narrowed and hard.

segs.t: A claw came at her face. She ducked under it and fired up through the opening chest.
Weeks of empty places,
she thought.
Dead ground, at night, where nobody saw my face. Then this morning, the Academy. Now.
By day, under every camera in the city.
So they would all see me with the Enders. And their suits run on belief.
Two more came from the left. She put one down. The other’s claw caught her shoulder and spun her around.
It sent me where she would follow.
This morning the order and her own wish had pointed at the same girl. She had not asked why.
I brought her here.
Then the purge order, with her standing in front of me. Kill my partner, or show my side.
Either way, it won.
Obsidia’s voice came back to her, from among the rows in the nest.
“If it ever slips beyond control, there is only one outcome,” Obsidia had said, of something she had made.
“Termination,” Vexana had answered. Even then she had heard it about herself.
Then let it use me,
she had thought, in her first hours in the dark.
It had. One instrument, spent, cost it nothing.
It never needed me loyal,
she thought.
It needed me used.
The ring closed again.
They were never mine. They only left me alone while I was useful.
She fought with one arm. Each shot from the staff punched a hole in their line, and the line closed again.

media.alt: Vexana fights the Enders alone across the ruined platform, firing her staff from the ground, leaping and striking; then bursts of violet light break around her as she fires into them.

segs.t: Far below the platforms, her giants lay in the rubble where they had fallen. Their swords lay across the stones beside them. She reached for them with what power she had.
One pair of eyes flickered yellow, and went out.
They needed her power poured into them without a break. She had none to spare. Every scrap went into the next shot.
They would never turn on her. They could not get up for her either.
She let them go.
A tall gray Ender came at her from the front. She set her boots wide on the stone.
Her father had stood like this once, in a street by the wall, with one Ender in front of him and his daughter behind.
“That Ender never got past him,” a soldier had told her, beside her cot. “Not while he stood.”
Her burned hand came away from her ribs and out to her side, flat and still. It hurt. She left it there.
Not while I stand,
thought Vexana.
“Dissolve into the dark of night.”
The shot took it through the chest.
Another claw laid her robe open from the shoulder, and she went down on one knee. She rose, and fired, and fired again.
The last Ender fell across her boots.
She stood in a ring of gray wreckage. Her breath was loud in her own ears. The arm at her side shook, and she let it fall.
Far off, the sirens of the city went on.
Then light came down through the clouds in beams. The clouds tore apart and cleared, fast, from the middle out.
The star in the sky stood wider than before. The Mother Matrix stepped out of it, whole.
Now she saw all of it. The horned head under its crown of spikes. Two violet eyes, glowing. Wings that opened and cut the beams of light to pieces. A chest shut tight, plate over plate.

media.alt: A vast dark armored shape towers against violet light and storm cloud, its crowned head high in the glare, huge clawed wings spread wide and its chest shut.

segs.t: Those eyes had looked down at her once, out of the torn sky over the tree.
Whole, and close. For weeks in the dark she had waited for this moment. Her plan had been made for nothing else.
It was looking straight at her.
She had nothing gathered. The Enders had taken it, shot by shot.
The seams of its chest plates began to glow. They split. In the gap a magenta core blazed.
The shot hit her before she could move.
She flew back across the stone. She struck it, rolled, and something cracked in her ribs.

media.alt: Through violet smoke a ring of magenta light swells in the sky above Vexana; then she is hurled backward and lies small among the broken stone of the ruined city.

segs.t: For a while everything was far off.
She found the staff by feel. She got it under her and rose to one knee. Her thumb found the brass collar on the grip, where it always sat.
She did not run. There was nowhere to run.
It opens when it strikes,
she thought. The first rule of Enders. When it fired again, the plates would split, and the core would be bare.
She pulled everything she had left into the orb. It came slowly, from far down. The black of the orb tightened and darkened, until it held a hard dark-pink knot.
When the chest opened, she would go into it with all of this. For humanity. For Guinevere.
Above her, white light gathered again behind the plates of its chest.
